interest: This file offers historians a unique operational register of how the U.S. State Department, War Department, and Navy Department monitored the worldwide movements of the Imperial Japanese Navy in the critical eighteen months preceding the attack on Pearl Harbor and into early 1942. Of particular diplomatic and strategic interest is the extensive documentation surrounding the special mission of the armed auxiliary transport Asaka Maru to Portugal, revealing high-stakes Allied deliberations over Canal transit security, armed guards versus liaison officers, and British contraband blockade enforcement against Axis passengers and cargo. Additionally, the docket provides a granular chronology of Japanese southern expansion into French Indochina, the Gulf of Siam, and the South China Sea, as well as global naval reconnaissance extending to the coasts of Peru and the Red Sea. Because the underlying classified and cross-referenced records were dispersed across military and diplomatic files, this List of Papers serves as an indispensable roadmap to prewar naval intelligence and diplomatic crisis management.
overview: This file comprises the U.S. State Department's decimal file 894.33 (File 179) docket sheets, designated 'List of Papers' (Form DS-46), recording communications, intelligence reports, and cross-references regarding the movements of Japanese naval vessels and foreign naval visits between May 1940 and June 1942. The compiled entries track the strategic deployment and reconnaissance of the Imperial Japanese Navy across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, and globally leading up to and during World War II. A major focus of the papers concerns the voyage of the Japanese armed naval transport Asaka (Asaka Maru) en route to Lisbon via the Panama Canal, including diplomatic negotiations over U.S. security inspections, transit conditions, British naval blockade restrictions on Axis goods, and the transport of Japanese military officials to Berlin. Additional intelligence entries document Japanese submarine movements near Hainan, the Philippines, the Red Sea, and Peru; naval and air buildups in French Indochina (Saigon, Cam Ranh Bay), Thailand, and Bias Bay; fleet concentrations off Japan and the Pacific Mandates; and Axis maritime coordination.

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entries 15 through 21 concerning Japanese naval movements and early transit plans for the naval transport Asaka.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (Form DS-46) records incoming and outgoing communications between May 1940 and January 1941 regarding Japanese naval operations. Items include reports from the Navy Department on fleet movements near Palau and home waters, intelligence on fifteen Japanese submarines dispatched to Hainan, and initial diplomatic notifications regarding the voyage of the armed transport Asaka to Lisbon via the Panama Canal. It also notes a departmental circular instructing American consuls to report on large Japanese merchant and naval vessels.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 1 (Revised October 17, 1945)

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entries 15 through 21 on Japanese naval forces and the transport Asaka.
subfiles.summary: This sheet constitutes an earlier version of Sheet 1, cataloguing documents from May 1940 through January 1941 under subject 894.33. It logs reports on Japanese naval forces moving toward Palau, press conference statements by Secretary Hull on fleet movements to French Indochina, and intelligence on submarines at Hainan. It further tracks requests from the Japanese Embassy for the Asaka to transit the Panama Canal and the Navy Department's conditional approval.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 1 (October 12, 1945)

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entries 22 through 29 regarding Panama Canal transit arrangements for the Asaka and naval movements near Thailand.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records diplomatic and military exchanges from January and February 1941 concerning the Japanese special service vessel Asaka. It tracks Ambassador Grew's reports that the vessel was armed, along with Japanese protests against U.S. requirements for an armed transit guard in the Panama Canal and the resulting compromise to place liaison officers on board. It also records an official Thai announcement regarding the arrival of a Japanese destroyer to maintain communications between Bangkok and warships at Saigon.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 3

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entries 30 through 34 on Japanese naval movements in Southeast Asia and Canal courtesies for the Asaka.
subfiles.summary: This sheet catalogues communications from February 1941, beginning with Foreign Minister Matsuoka's appreciation for courtesies extended to the Asaka during its Panama Canal passage. It logs intelligence from Australian and Canadian diplomatic missions concerning Japanese fleet deployments in the Gulf of Siam, including naval occupation of Cam Ranh and Songkhla. It also records naval and troop movements around Bias Bay and staffing constraints reported by the American consulate in Hong Kong.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 4

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entries 35 through 43 on Japanese naval activities in Thailand, Hong Kong waters, and the Asaka's arrival in Europe.
subfiles.summary: This sheet logs communications from February 1941 regarding Japanese naval activities in Southeast Asia and Europe. It documents visits of Japanese destroyers to Paknam, Thailand, naval cruising in the Gulf of Siam, and warship operations in Bias Bay. It also tracks the arrival of the Asaka in Lisbon disembarking 111 military officials bound for Berlin, discussions with the British regarding refusal of Suez Canal passage, and U.S.-Japanese negotiations over Panama Canal regulations.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 5

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entries 44 through 54 regarding British blockade scrutiny of the Asaka Maru and warship movements in Saigon.
subfiles.summary: This sheet records communications from February and March 1941 concerning the Asaka Maru's passengers and cargo, highlighting British Foreign Office warnings against carrying German or Italian goods under blockade regulations. It tracks reports on the Japanese destroyer Isokaze replacing cruiser Abukuma at Saigon to evacuate bomber ground crews and repair equipment. Additional entries log sightings of the armed vessel Buenos Aires Maru in Porto Alegre, Australian reports on naval movements, and Japan's notification that the Asaka would not return via the Panama Canal.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 6

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entries 55 through 60 regarding legal aspects of the British blockade, Japanese withdrawal from Saigon, and maritime intelligence.
subfiles.summary: This sheet catalogues communications from February through April 1941 detailing diplomatic deliberations over British blockade interception of the Asaka Maru carrying Portuguese cargo to Japan, where the U.S. expressed legal reservations. It documents the departure of the destroyer Isokaze and bombers from Saigon, leaving only Colonel Saito and civilian assistants in Cochinchina. Other entries record naval attache reports on the Asaka's European mission, inquiries into military strategy regarding a surprise attack, and intelligence from an American tanker captain in Hong Kong.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 7

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entries 61 through 71 concerning worldwide Japanese naval movements, aircraft deployments, and submarine sightings.
subfiles.summary: This sheet catalogues communications spanning March 1941 to January 1942 regarding global Japanese naval movements and intelligence. Notable entries include customs searches of the Akagi Maru at Hilo, Coast Guard surveillance of the Asaka leaving Lisbon, and the arrival of Italian escort vessel Eritrea at Kobe. It further details intelligence on the Combined Fleet concentrating off Toyokawa, aircraft stationed in the Pacific Mandates, merchant shipping in the Pearl River, and reports of Japanese submarines off the Red Sea and Peru.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 8

subfiles.about: State Department docket sheet logging entry 72 regarding Spanish press statements on Axis submarine fueling.
subfiles.summary: This final docket sheet logs a telegram from Ambassador Carlton J. H. Hayes in Spain dated June 30, 1941. It reports that the Spanish Foreign Office summoned American, British, French, and Japanese press correspondents to deliver an official communication denying accusations that Spanish merchant ships were providing bunker fuel to Axis submarines. The document is cross-referenced to decimal file FW852.901/27.
subfiles.title: List of Papers, Sheet 9
